item.title: Space curves in Hahn calculus: rotation structure, a fundamental theorem, and $q$-deformed invariants at the fixed point
item.description: arXiv:2610.33084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop the differential geometry of space curves in Hahn's quantum calculus, where the derivative is the difference quotient along the contraction $\sigma(t)=qt+\omega$ with fixed point $\omega_0=\omega/(1-q)$. The Hahn Frenet frame is transported along every orbit of $\sigma$ by rotations through turning and torsion angles, which identifies it with the discrete Frenet frame of the inscribed orbit polygon. An embedded regular Hahn curve is determined, up to linear reparametrization about $\omega_0$, by its trace and the induced contraction. We prove a sharp planarity criterion and a fundamental theorem via an infinite product of rotations and the Jackson--N\"orlund integral. For smooth curves, expansions uniform in $q$ show that at $\omega_0$ the Hahn curvature and torsion carry the factors $[2]_q/2$ and $[3]_q/3$. These factors, a sampling effect of geometrically decaying steps, disappear under edge-length normalization, but their quotient persists in the limiting ratio of torsion and turning angles of every polygon inscribed in a smooth curve with monotonically converging vertices and edge lengths decaying with ratio~$q$. In uniformly sampled relaxation towards a stable node, the factors can become measurable biases. We characterize generalized Hahn helices by a two-step relation between turning and torsion angles; their Lancret ratio at $\omega_0$ is $\pm([2]_q/2)\cot\vartheta$, where $\vartheta$ is the helix angle. Unlike the classical case, a constant ratio of torsion and curvature does not characterize helices: curves with constant curvature and torsion are never generalized Hahn helices, and, near $\omega_0$, unit-speed helices with a given ratio are unique up to similarities and linear reparametrization.
item.dc:creator: Umut Selvi, Derya Sa\u{g}lam

item.title: Singular Atiyah Configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.33090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct arbitrarily large configurations of distinct points in Euclidean three-space with linearly dependent Atiyah polynomials, including planar configurations. The configurations consist of two coaxial cyclic orbits and axial points. We also obtain analogous configurations in hyperbolic three-space.
item.dc:creator: Jan Eickhoff

item.title: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.33261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a sphere other than the 4-sphere is regular. On even-dimensional spheres other than the 4-sphere we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics of non-constant curvature carrying Besse families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Christian Lange

item.title: Volume of area-bounded PGL3-Hitchin moduli space
item.description: arXiv:2610.33417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the $\mathrm{PGL}_3$-Hitchin moduli space of unmarked convex $\mathbb{RP}^2$ structures on the surface $S_{g,m}$ with fixed boundary data $\mathbf L$ when $m>0$, we investigate the subset whose canonical Hilbert--Busemann area is bounded above by $t$. We show that the Goldman symplectic volume of this subset is at most $C_{g,m}(t+\lambda^2)^{8g-8+3m}$, where $\lambda$ is the largest total-root boundary length for $m>0$ and is set to $0$ for $m=0$. As a consequence, We obtain the explicit upper bound for the $e^{-s\cdot\mathrm{Area}}$-weighted volume.
item.dc:creator: Qiongling Li, Beibei Liu, Weixu Su, Zhe Sun

item.title: Hitchin's $\alpha$-invariant and positive sectional curvature on homotopy $9$-spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.33474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a smooth homotopy $9$-sphere admits a Riemannian metric of positive sectional curvature if and only if its Hitchin $\alpha$-invariant vanishes, or equivalently if and only if it admits a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature.
item.dc:creator: Yang-Hui He, Ziran Liu, Shing-Tung Yau

item.title: Multi-marginal optimal transport on sub-Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.33721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study multi-marginal optimal transport on ideal sub-Riemannian manifolds. We establish a sub-Riemannian barycentric balance condition and prove the existence of a solution to the Monge problem under an additional assumption. We also investigate the absolute continuity of Wasserstein barycenters. Our results extend and improve upon those of Pass, Pinamonti, and Vedovato (Methods Appl. Anal. 28 (2021), 61-76) on the Heisenberg group, answering two open questions raised in their work.
item.dc:creator: Haowei Lin

item.title: Price's law for scalar waves on 1+4 dimensional subextremal Myers-Perry spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.33812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Myers--Perry spacetimes $(M,g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}})$ in $1+4$ dimensions with two spin parameters $(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b})\in\mathbb{R}^2$, which are a direct generalization of the well known Kerr spacetime in $1+3$ dimensions. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow associated to $g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}^{-1}$ is normally hyperbolically trapped for the full subextremal range \[ (|\mathbf{a}|+|\mathbf{b}|)^2<2\mathfrak{m}. \] As an application, we prove a Price law with explicit leading order terms for solutions $\phi(t,x)$ of the scalar wave equation \[ \Box_{g_{\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathfrak{m}}}\phi=0 \] under the assumption of real mode stability. Our precise asymptotics imply that $\phi(t,x)=ct^{-3}+\mathcal{O}(t^{-4+})$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}$ is an explicitly computable constant.
item.dc:creator: Pieter-Bart Peters

item.title: Extrinsic Curvature Estimation by Closest Point Projection of Rays
item.description: arXiv:2610.33943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a parametrization-free framework for estimating the second fundamental form and the principal curvatures of a submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^d$. The method uses the closest point projections of a few short random rays and recovers the curvature from the curves that these projections induce on the submanifold, without coordinate charts or local fitting. We analyze the geometry of the induced curves and characterize when they are geodesics. For hypersurfaces, these results give two algorithms with error bounds: a least squares reconstruction of the second fundamental form from the curvatures of the induced curves, and a direct estimate of all principal curvatures from the eigenvalues of a $d\times d$ matrix built from $d$ rays, which needs no normal information and costs $\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ besides the projections. In higher codimension, we can also recover the second fundamental form one normal direction at a time. On point clouds, where the projection becomes a nearest neighbor query, we bound the additional error. Experiments confirm the predicted rates for hypersurfaces in up to $128$ dimensions, for surfaces of codimension up to $98$, and on point clouds, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework in practice.
item.dc:creator: Liangchen Liu, Yen-Hsi Richard Tsai

item.title: A note on $\sigma_k$ maximal conformal volume
item.description: arXiv:2610.33986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a sharp spherical upper bound for the $\sigma_k$-maximal conformal volume $\Lambda_k$ introduced by Gursky and Viaclovsky. Let $(M^n,[g])$ be a smooth, closed, connected conformal manifold with $n\geq 3$ and $n/2<k\leq n$, and suppose that $[g]$ contains a $k$-admissible metric, we prove that $ \Lambda_k(M,[g]) \leq \operatorname{Vol}(\mathbb S^n,g_{\mathrm{rd}}), $ with equality if and only if $(M,[g])$ is conformally equivalent to the standard sphere. Combined with the existence and compactness theorem of Gursky and Viaclovsky below the spherical threshold, this completes their approach to the $\sigma_k$-Yamabe problem through maximal conformal volume in the range $k>n/2$.
item.dc:creator: Mijia Lai

item.title: A simple construction of smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carath\'eodory conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2610.34036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alp\"oge recently announced smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carath\'eodory conjectures. We present a simpler construction based on a trigonometric function as a seed. Using this, for every positive integer $k$, we construct a smooth real-valued function on the plane, flat at the origin, whose Hessian eigenline fields have an isolated singularity of index $1+k/2$. A support-function parametrization realizes this index as an umbilic index of a non-real analytic $C^\infty$-regular surface germ in Euclidean $3$-space. The same framework, applied to a rapidly decreasing function on the whole plane, gives a strictly convex closed smooth surface with exactly one umbilic, of index $2$. This paper is self-contained with regard to the existence of an umbilic of index $2$ and the construction of a counterexample to the Carath\'eodory conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Naoya Ando, Masaaki Umehara

item.title: Refined analysis on finite-time singularities of almost-holomorphic harmonic map flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.34132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on the work of Song--Waldron~\cite{SongWaldron2024}, we establish stronger regularity and refined blow-up analysis results for almost-holomorphic harmonic map flow from a closed surface into a compact K\"ahler manifold with nonnegative holomorphic bisectional curvature. At each finite-time singularity, we improve the outer energy scale to $O((T-t)/\sqrt{|\ln(T-t)|})$. We also prove that both the stress-energy tensor and the tension field converge strongly in $L^2$ to those of the body map, by ruling out concentration of their $L^2$ energy near the singular points. Consequently, the body map belongs to $W^{2,2}$. Finally, an explicit gap theorem for the antiholomorphic energy of nonholomorphic harmonic spheres yields an explicit admissible threshold for the initial antiholomorphic energy under which these conclusions hold.
item.dc:creator: Yihan He, Ze Li, Chong Song

item.title: K-energy for the coupled constant scalar curvature K\"{a}hler equation, I: Slope formula and semistability
item.description: arXiv:2610.34145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study coupled constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics defined by Datar-Pingali extending coupled K\"ahler-Einstein metrics defined by Hultgren-Witt Nystr\"om. We consider two K-energy functionals of which one (denoted $\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ccscK}}$) integrates the moment map considered by Datar-Pingali and the other (denoted $\mathcal{M}'$) is designed so that its slope at infinity for subgeodesic rays for ample test configurations with reduced central fiber coincides with the Donaldson-Futaki invariant considered by Hultgren-Witt Nystr\"om and Datar-Pingali. We also extend $\mathcal{M}_{\operatorname{ccscK}}$ to $\mathcal{H}^{1,\bar{1}}$ and the finite energy class $\mathcal{E}^1$, and prove its convexity along tuples of weak geodesics and finite energy geodesics, respectively. As a corollary, we obtain a semistability condition necessary for the existence of ccscK metrics.
item.dc:creator: Akito Futaki, Jianwei Shi

item.title: Sharp gradient comparison and rigidity for semilinear equations on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.34207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sharp amplitude and gradient comparisons for positive solutions of a class of semilinear elliptic equations on complete manifolds under a Ricci lower bound. Equality at one point characterizes hyperbolic space and the corresponding radial solution. The local estimates are uniform in the mixing coefficients and number of terms for positive mixtures of subcritical powers. For a class of conformal compactifications defined by a source equation, we obtain sharp boundary scalar-curvature bounds and hyperbolic rigidity. We also construct non-Einstein examples whose normalization persists under small compactly supported metric perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Linlin Sun

item.title: Clifford-weighted residues, partial spectral curvature, and torsion
item.description: arXiv:2610.34256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Clifford-weighted noncommutative residues associated with Dirac operators and connections. On closed spin manifolds a double commutator of the square of the Dirac operator, paired with a Clifford commutator, recovers the localized Riemann curvature tensor. We prove presentation independence for its extension to arbitrary classical one-forms, recompute four-Clifford functionals, and give explicit Weyl, Schouten and Einstein curvature combinations. For spectral triples with an admissible residue calculus we define a partial spectral curvature functional on two arbitrary represented one-forms and two exact represented one-forms. Its well-definedness is distinguished from module tensoriality: explicit flat noncommutative-torus computations exhibit both a failure of general presentation descent and nonzero partial pairings. A connection-based curvature pairing provides a separate construction, including noncentral pure Clifford-degree-two examples. We also derive ordered first- and second-derivative torsion residues on free torus modules and prove an obstruction to ordinary alternation for unrestricted noncentral inputs. All constants, coefficient orders and hypotheses are kept explicit.
item.dc:creator: Yong Wang

item.title: Length bounds and rigidity for ancient curve shortening flow on warped product surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.34274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study ancient solutions to curve shortening flow on a class of warped product surfaces. For closed embedded ancient solutions whose curves are not null-homotopic, we prove that graphicality at every time is equivalent to a uniform length bound as $t\to-\infty$, and that these properties hold whenever the length is $o(\sqrt{-t})$. Under an additional positivity condition on the linearized height equation, every such solution with bounded length is a family of slices. We derive backward convergence to a limiting circle from the length bound and prove slice rigidity by an $L^2$ estimate for the height perturbation.
item.dc:creator: Beomseok Goh, Taehun Lee

item.title: Small eigenvalues of negatively curved manifolds with finite volume
item.description: arXiv:2610.34337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain upper bounds for the number of small eigenvalues of complete Riemannian manifolds with negative sectional curvature and finite volume.
item.dc:creator: Werner Ballmann, Panagiotis Polymerakis

item.title: Pseudo-Calabi Flow on Toric Variety
item.description: arXiv:2610.34340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove the long time existence of the pseudo-Calabi flow on a compact toric variety for any $T^n$-invariant initial K\"ahler metric. If the Mabuchi functional is proper modulo automorphisms, the flow converges exponentially to a constant scalar curvature K\"ahler (cscK) metric. In particular, this gives a flow proof that properness of the K-energy implies the existence of a cscK metric in the toric setting.
item.dc:creator: Junhao Tian, Kai Zheng

item.title: Sharp diameter estimates via integral geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.34367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the diameter of a closed embedded surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is always less than the integral of the magnitude of the mean curvature, divided by $\pi$. We also prove a sharp variant for surfaces with boundary, and apply it to address a conjecture of Miura.
item.dc:creator: Peter M. Topping

item.title: Chern holonomy under the first and second Chern--Ricci flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.34665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare the Chern holonomy of the first and second Chern-Ricci flows on compact complex manifolds. For the first flow, we construct an explicit immortal pluriclosed solution on a complex two-torus with full and restricted holonomy $U(2)$, except at one finite time when both groups are $U(1)^2$; its smooth limit has holonomy $SU(2)$. The solution is uniformly nondegenerate and has bounds of every fixed differential order for all time. In contrast, the second Chern-Ricci flow preserves full and restricted Chern holonomy under the natural unitary identification, including the initial time and nonclosed groups. The proof combines preservation of a connection reduction, positive-time analyticity, and a path-transport comparison. As an application, the optimal minimum mean curvature on a holomorphic bundle is unchanged when metrics are restricted to any realizable full and restricted holonomy class. An explicit projected-curvature source explains the failure of the corresponding Ricci-flow holonomy argument.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Liao

item.title: Constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature on two-step solvmanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.34820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M=\Gamma\backslash G$ be a compact solvmanifold with a left-invariant Hermitian structure whose Lie algebra is two-step solvable. If the Chern holomorphic sectional curvature is constant, then the derived algebra is $J$-invariant and the Chern connection is flat. At the Lie-algebra level, we also prove that constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature is impossible for a unimodular two-step solvable Hermitian Lie algebra of mixed Freibert-Swann type.
item.dc:creator: Shanlin Guan, Yuqin Guo

item.title: A complete parameter classification of left-invariant Bott affine Ricci solitons for two rotated distributions on three-dimensional Lorentzian Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.34835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all left-invariant affine Ricci solitons associated with the Bott connections of two fixed rank-two distributions on the seven standard families of three-dimensional Lorentzian Lie groups. The distributions are defined by a fixed orthogonal change of the spacelike frame. A universal adapted-frame calculation provides explicit connection matrices, curvature operators and the symmetrized Ricci tensor. The equation in the orthogonal-complement direction forces every left-invariant solution to be steady. The remaining equations yield elementary parameter families and finitely many real algebraic branches: four normalized branches for $G_2$, six branches for each sign parameter in $G_4$, and two quartic branches in $G_7$ in addition to its elementary families. Resultants, subresultants, exact polynomial reduction and Sturm root isolation establish necessity, sufficiency and exhaustiveness. Degenerate cases are treated separately, including all families with nonunique soliton vector fields. An invertible frame transformation relates the two distribution problems. The classification is in the stated structure parameters; no quotient by isometries, automorphisms or scaling is taken.
item.dc:creator: Fanqi Lin

item.title: Embedded minimal surfaces with three ends associated with the Hoffman-Osserman catenoids
item.description: arXiv:2610.34856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every positive integer $g$ and every Hoffman-Osserman catenoid in $\mathbb{R}^5$, we construct a complete embedded minimal surface of genus $g$ that is not contained in any proper affine subspace of $\mathbb{R}^5$. These surfaces can be viewed as higher-codimensional analogues of the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces, associated with the union of the corresponding Hoffman-Osserman catenoid and the plane containing its waist circle. We provide explicit Weierstrass data for these surfaces. Our construction can also be interpreted as restoring conformality to a deformed Costa-Hoffman-Meeks immersion by introducing two additional harmonic coordinate functions.
item.dc:creator: Jaehoon Lee, Eungbeom Yeon

item.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.35000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture for closed mean curvature flows. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean curvature flows with prescribed tangent flows (arXiv:2405.15577, arXiv:2607.23879) and the noncompact counterexample (arXiv:2605.09657) gives the desired examples.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Chen

item.title: Singular Limits of Frame Bundles of Noncollapsing Positively Curved Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.35146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each dimension $n\ge 2$, we construct noncollapsing sequences of metrics on $S^n$ with a uniform positive lower bound on sectional curvature whose oriented orthonormal frame bundles, equipped with the canonically induced connection metrics, converge to nonmanifold metric spaces homeomorphic to $\Sigma(S^{n-1}\times\SO(n))$. In even dimensions, real projective quotients give connected full frame bundles with the same limits, disproving the manifold conclusion in Yamaguchi's frame bundle conjecture. In odd dimensions, each component of the full projective frame bundle, with its intrinsic metric, converges to the quotient of the spherical limit by a free involution. The singularities are detected by local homology, and we obtain quantitative equivariant Gromov--Hausdorff estimates. We also compare the frame bundle limits with the intrinsic completions of their regular limiting frame metrics, and present and discuss alternatives to Yamaguchi's original conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Chao Qian, Wilderich Tuschmann

item.title: Bach-flat metrics and global regularity of conformal structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.35257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study global regularity properties of conformal structures on compact manifolds with applications to conformally invariant variational problems. We find sharp conditions ensuring that a manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric of Sobolev class is conformally diffeomorphic to a smooth one. In particular, we prove that $W^{2,q}$ Bach-flat four-manifolds with $q > 2$ are smooth up to conformal diffeomorphisms. We also solve the Yamabe problem for $W^{2,q}$ metrics with $q > 2$ on three-manifolds under a mild conformal condition.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Avalos, Albachiara Cogo, Andoni Royo Abrego

item.title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.35383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a relative BFK gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to L\"uck and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles.
item.dc:creator: Victor Kalvin

item.title: The quermassintegral inequalities for k-convex spiral-star-shaped domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.35394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the quermassintegral inequalities of our earlier work \cite{GuanLi2009} from star-shaped domains to a substantially broader class of domains in Euclidean space, which we call spiral-star-shaped. A smooth domain is spiral-star-shaped if its boundary satisfies \[ \langle X+A X,\nu\rangle>0 \] for some fixed skew-symmetric linear map $ A$, where $X$ is the position vector and $\nu$ is the outward unit normal. The vector field $X+A X$ is conformal Killing, with dilation component $X$ and rotational component $A X$; its trajectories combine expansion and rotation, giving rise to the spiral terminology. When $A=0$, it reduces to ordinary star-shapedness, while nonzero $A$ allows domains that are not star-shaped in the usual radial sense. For smooth $k$-convex spiral-star-shaped domains, we prove long-time existence and exponential convergence to a round sphere for a locally constrained inverse curvature flow. The positive spiral support function provides the geometric control needed to treat initial hypersurfaces that need not be star-shaped in the usual sense. Monotonicity of the quermassintegrals along the flow yields sharp quermassintegral inequalities in this enlarged class, with equality if and only if the domain is a ball.
item.dc:creator: Junfang Li

item.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ denote the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces with $n$ cusps. We obtain an asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the genus as $g\to\infty$, uniformly for all $n\ge0$. This includes cusp counts of order $\sqrt g$ and larger, where the fixed-$n$ expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf no longer gives a uniform approximation. The leading term is explicit and has relative error $O(g^{-1})$. Truncating the expansion at a suitably chosen order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$, with no restriction on the growth of $n$. For fixed $n$, the leading term identifies the universal constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics as $1/\sqrt\pi$, as conjectured by Zograf. We also answer two questions of Mirzakhani: we determine explicit asymptotic profiles for volume ratios uniformly in the number of cusps, and for adjacent coefficient ratios of the one-boundary volume polynomial uniformly over all degrees. The proof uses a positive recursion for mixed $\kappa_1$--$\psi$ intersection numbers, with the absolute normalization determined by comparison with the known asymptotics of pure $\psi$ intersection numbers.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyi Li, Qihang Wang

item.title: Pure Type-One Generalized Hypercomplex Structures in Dimension Four
item.description: arXiv:2610.35557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify untwisted generalized hypercomplex structures on four-manifolds whose entire sphere has type one. The three Poisson tensors determine a canonical line field, and the local data are Gauduchon--Tod coframes. We determine local equivalence under diffeomorphisms, common closed real $B$-fields and constant rotations of the triple. On a closed manifold the canonical foliation is automatically Riemannian: a nonzero period obstructs the exact twist required by the non-Riemannian models. The compact structures form four families, distinguished by $b_1=1,2,3,4$: Berger quotients, flat axis quotients, nontrivial circle bundles over flat three-tori, and constant tori. We determine their parameters, equivalences and finite ordered quotients, including nonorientable canonical lines. The underlying manifolds are parallelizable, satisfy $b_2=2b_1-2$, and are symplectic exactly when the intrinsic Gauduchon--Tod invariant vanishes. A twisted Hopf example shows why the untwisted hypothesis is essential. The classification is intrinsic and assumes no initial circle action. These results address the four-dimensional untwisted case of the intermediate-type question of Fino and Grantcharov.
item.dc:creator: Guangzhen Ren

item.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.35651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As a consequence, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Dorofeev, Alexander Pigazzini

item.title: Curvature quotient flows and Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2610.35707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quermassintegral-preserving curvature flows in $\mathbb H^{n+1}$, $n\geq3$, driven by the curvature quotient $(E_k/E_\ell)^{1/(k-\ell)}$. For $1\leq\ell<k$ with $k+\ell\leq n$, we prove that positive sectional curvature is preserved. Starting from a smooth closed strictly convex hypersurface with positive sectional curvature, the flow exists for all time and converges smoothly and exponentially to a geodesic sphere. As an application, we establish sharp Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities between $W_k$ and $W_\ell$ for smooth bounded convex domains whose boundaries have nonnegative sectional curvature, whenever $0\leq\ell<k\leq n$ and $k+\ell\leq n$. Equality holds if and only if the domain is a geodesic ball. Together with previously known cases, these inequalities give the full family of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for this class of domains in $\mathbb H^6$. We also construct counterexamples showing that $k+\ell\leq n$ is the optimal range for preservation of positive sectional curvature by these flows.
item.dc:creator: Tianci Luo, Yong Wei, Ruijia Zhang, Rong Zhou

item.title: Yang-Mills-Higgs Limits of Reflexive Higgs Sheaves
item.description: arXiv:2610.35742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For stable Higgs bundles, Hermitian-Einstein metrics can be obtained as limits of the Yang-Mills-Higgs (Y-M-H) flow. We study the algebraic structure of subsequential limits of this flow for reflexive Higgs sheaves over compact K\"ahler manifolds, without assuming stability. We prove that the limiting reflexive Higgs sheaf is isomorphic to the double dual of the graded sheaf associated with the Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration of the initial sheaf.
item.dc:creator: Tianshu Jiang, Yijian Zhang

item.title: The Weyl Problem for Planar CBB$(-1)$ Surfaces in Hyperbolic $3$-Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.35744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the Weyl problem for noncompact convex surfaces in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$. We prove that any planar CBB$(-1)$ surface with countably many ends can be isometrically embedded as the boundary of a closed convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{H}^3$ such that each connected component of the ideal boundary of $X$ is either a round disk or a single point. By known rigidity results, such an embedding is unique up to isometries of $\mathbb{H}^3$. Moreover, we show that the assumption of countably many ends can be dropped if Koebe's circle domain conjecture holds.
item.dc:creator: Xinrong Zhao

item.title: Properly embedded Legendrian surfaces in the tangent sphere bundle of hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2610.35812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that every open Riemann surface may be conformally properly embedded in the tangent sphere bundle of hyperbolic $3$-space as a Legendrian surface. We achieve this by constructing proper holomorphic Legendrian embeddings in $\mathrm{SL}_2 (\mathbb{C})$ whose projections to the quotient $\mathrm{SL}_2 (\mathbb{C})/ \mathrm{U}_1$ remain embeddings. As another consequence, every open Riemann surface admits a proper holomorphic Legendrian embedding in the projectivised special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_2 (\mathbb{C})$.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Hidalgo

item.title: Morse index characterization of the Veronese projective plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.35820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Following Simons' seminal work in 1968, every closed, connected, embedded minimal surface in the four-sphere that is not totally geodesic has Morse index at least five. In this paper, we prove that equality holds if and only if the surface is congruent to the Veronese projective plane. Relying on recent advances by Bernstein and Ketover, this characterization settles Kusner's 1996 conjecture on the minimizers of the Willmore functional in dimension four for surfaces whose normal bundle has nonzero Euler number. This is always the case, in particular, for embeddings of nonorientable surfaces whose orientation double cover has even genus.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Carlotto, Yangyang Li, Zhihan Wang

item.title: Nonabelian Higgs fields from minimal submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.35837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills-Higgs fields on a broad class of noncompact Riemannian manifolds, concentrating in the large-mass limit along prescribed nondegenerate minimal submanifolds of codimension three. The solutions have uniformly bounded rescaled energy. On closed manifolds with $b_1(M)=0$, adding a suitably scaled Higgs potential gives an analogous concentration result. Our construction completes one direction of the correspondence proposed by Parise, Pigati and Stern, realising prescribed minimal submanifolds of codimension three as concentration sets of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Higgs fields.
item.dc:creator: Marco Badran

item.title: Delambre--Gauss Formulas in Complex Hyperbolic Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.33468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a Delambre--Gauss matrix identity for oriented right-angled hexagons in the complex hyperbolic plane. The six complex length parameters of a hexagon determine two alternating \(3\times3\) matrices whose product is central in (\mathrm{SU}(2,1)\). The resulting nine entry-wise equations extend the Delambre-Gauss formula of Tan, Wong, and Zhang in 4-dimensional hyperbolic geometry to this complex hyperbolic setting.
item.dc:creator: Jiming Ma, Baohua Xie

item.title: Blow-up analysis and compactness for critical Dirac equations on $\mathbb S^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.33507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study blow-up and compactness for the critical nonlinear Dirac equation \[ D_{g_0}\psi_i = H_i|\psi_i|^{\frac{2}{n-1}}\psi_i \qquad \text{on }\mathbb S^n,\quad n\ge 3, \] where $g_0$ is the round metric and $H_i\to H>0$ in $C^0(\mathbb S^n)$. Under a first-threshold bound on the critical mass, we prove that every blowing-up sequence has, after passing to a subsequence, a unique blow-up point $p$ satisfying $H(p)=\max_{\mathbb S^n}H$. The rescaled solutions converge to a ground-state Dirac bubble that carries the entire limiting critical mass. Under local uniform $C^1$ bounds on $H_i$, we use the Kelvin transform and a second rescaling to prove that $p$ is an isolated simple blow-up point. We also derive sharp pointwise and gradient estimates in cylindrical coordinates and identify the normalized Green limit. If the coefficients converge in $C^2$ near $p$, the Pohozaev identity yields $\operatorname{Hess}_{g_0}H(p)=0$. Consequently, if a positive $H\in C^2(\mathbb S^n)$ satisfies $\Delta_{g_0}H(p)<0$ at every global maximum, then solutions with critical mass bounded by a level slightly above the first threshold are uniformly bounded in $L^\infty(\mathbb S^n)$. This bound remains uniform under small $C^2$ perturbations of $H$.
item.dc:creator: Ting Li, Zhongwei Tang

item.title: An Elliptic Path Fibration and Holomorphic Morita Equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2610.33793v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an elliptic analogue of the Alekseev-Meinrenken path fibration \cite{alekseev2009atiyah} for a simply connected complex Lie group with a nondegenerate invariant symmetric bilinear form. A natural $2$-form on the correspondence space induces a holomorphic symplectic groupoid over the space of $(0,1)$-connections and a holomorphic quasi-symplectic groupoid over the holomorphic loop group. The correspondence space defines a principal holomorphic Morita bibundle with compatible differential forms.
item.dc:creator: Ahmmadreza Khazaeipoul

item.title: Critical metrics for the Dirac-Yamabe eigenvalue ratio and Einstein-Dirac equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.33825v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 3$ with positive Yamabe constant. We prove that critical metrics for the mixed eigenvalue ratio $\mathcal H(g)=\frac{\lambda_1(D_g)^2}{\lambda_1(L_g)},$ where $D_g$ is the Dirac operator and $L_g$ is the conformal Laplacian are characterized by a harmonic section whose energy-momentum tensor satisfies an Einstein--Dirac equation. We discuss consequences of this result for Hijazi's inequality, and we construct an example to prove that $\mathcal H$ is unbounded above within the conformal class of the round sphere.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Eddaoudi

item.title: Nilpotent Lie algebras of nilpotence class at most three via graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.33963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we associate with each finite simple graph $G$ a nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}_G$ of class at most three, whose underlying vector space has a basis indexed by the vertices, edges, and paths of length two of $G$. Its nilpotency class is exactly three if and only if $G$ contains a path of length two. We compute the dimensions of its lower central series and describe its center. Over fields of characteristic different from two, we prove that two such Lie algebras are isomorphic if and only if their underlying graphs are isomorphic. We also give an algebraic description using quotients involving exterior and symmetric squares. Finally, we study balanced blow-ups and prove that $\mathfrak{n}_G$ is a retract of $\mathfrak{n}_{G^{(m)}}$.
item.dc:creator: Andrea L. Gallo, Denis E. Videla

item.title: The Genus-One B-Model Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg Correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2610.33984v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. The Calabi--Yau/Landau--Ginzburg correspondence predicts a close relation between invariants of the Landau--Ginzburg orbifold $(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb Z_n,f)$ and those of the associated Calabi--Yau hypersurface $ X_f=\{[z_1:\cdots:z_n]\in\mathbb P^{n-1}:f(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=0\}. $ In this paper, we establish this correspondence for the genus-one B-model by constructing the Landau--Ginzburg genus-one B-model invariant intrinsically from the $f$-twisted Laplacian on $\mathbb{C}^n/\mathbb{Z}_n$ and proving that it agrees with the corresponding BCOV invariant of $X_f$ up to an additive constant depending only on the dimension.
item.dc:creator: Xinxing Tang, Junrong Yan

item.title: Symplectic capacities and Weyl laws from Abelian Higgs min max theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.34062v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a Hermitian line bundle $E\to Y$ over a Riemannian manifold $(Y^n,g)$, the self-dual Abelian--Higgs energy is defined by $ \En^Y_{\eps,g}(u,a)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_Y \left(|\nabla_a u|_g^2+\eps^2|F_a|_g^2+ \frac{(1-|u|^2)^2}{4\eps^2}\right)dV_g, $ where $u$ is a smooth section of $E$, $a$ is a unitary connection, and $F_a$ is its curvature. Pigati and Stern studied the energy as a codimension-two analogue of the Allen--Cahn energy to study minimal submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold. In this paper, we use this functional to define a nondecreasing sequence of symplectic capacities $\{c_k^{\AH}\}_{k\ge1}$ in dimension four by a min--max construction. In particular, we prove that $c_1^{\AH}$ is normalized on the ball and the cylinder. For the upper bound on the cylinder, we combine Gromov's theory of families of $J$-holomorphic spheres with Taubes's planar vortex. For the lower bound on the ball, we use the properties of the Abelian--Higgs theory developed by Pigati--Stern, together with a geometric estimate on smooth approximations to the double of the ball and an equivariant deformation of low energy sublevels. These estimates give the normalization without Seiberg--Witten theory. We then use Seiberg--Witten moduli spaces on $\CP^2$ and $S^2\times S^2$ to prove an upper bound on the higher capacities of balls and the formula $c_k^{\AH}(Z^4(a),\omega_0)=ka$. We also prove Euclidean Weyl laws for the capacity sequence and for the min--max sequence with the standard Euclidean metric. For these results, we construct AH sweepouts from moduli spaces of the solutions to the perturbed Seiberg--Witten equations.
item.dc:creator: Taisuke Shibata

item.title: Equivariant Poisson structures on moment-angle manifolds and their quotients
item.description: arXiv:2610.34090v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct several families of torus equivariant Poisson structures on moment-angle manifolds and their quotients such as quasitoric manifolds. We study the symplectic foliation and Poisson cohomology groups associated with these structures.
item.dc:creator: Vansh Aggarwal, Mainak Poddar

item.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincar\'e prior that neither test decides
item.description: arXiv:2610.34309v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $\delta_F$ is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincar\'e inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincar\'e, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincar\'e class the zone is two-sided: the same circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Roshka

item.title: Positive solutions of Yamabe-type equations with general potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.34417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$, and let $\psi\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. We prove that the equation $$ -\frac{4(n-1)}{n-2}\Delta_g u+\psi u=u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} $$ has a smooth positive solution if and only if its linear part has positive first eigenvalue. In dimensions $n\ge6$, the proof combines an energy estimate under exact local mass constraints with an intersection argument for finite cycles of atomic measures; dimensions $3\le n\le5$ follow from the theorem of Bahri and Brezis.
item.dc:creator: Hongyu Chen, Li Ma

item.title: Existence of static axisymmetric solutions to the Einstein equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34555v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct smooth Riemannian metrics and scalar potentials that are invariant under a circle action and satisfy the static Einstein equations with positive cosmological constant. The underlying compact three-manifold is a ball with two disjoint open balls removed. The potential (or lapse function) is positive in the interior and vanishes at the boundary, consisting of three non-degenerate horizons. The areas of the two inner boundary components are controlled by two arbitrary parameters, namely the masses of the black holes, which are taken to be sufficiently small and comparable. Each inner horizon radius scales linearly with the individual mass parameters, while the separation of their reference centers scales as the cube root of the total mass. These two scales are assumed to be sufficiently small at different rates, whereas the cosmological length remains fixed. The main analytical challenge is to control the linearized equation and the nonlinear remainder simultaneously near the shrinking horizons, between the centers and in the outer region. Weighted H\"older estimates quantify the growth of the inverse and show that the error of an approximation joining Kottler collars to de Sitter space is small enough to close a contraction argument. Namely, we solve a reduced elliptic Einstein equation that is endowed with two obstruction tensors; varying the two axial positions removes their coefficients. The contracted Bianchi identity and an energy estimate for an auxiliary vector field (Killing field) introduced by the projection to vanish. Finally, for a fixed cosmological constant, the intrinsic metric of one of the two boundary components is sufficient to determine a static solution with simply connected interior and non-vanishing boundary gradient, up to isometry and multiplication of the potential by a positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Philippe G. LeFloch, Luc Rozoy

item.title: Aspherical Symplectic Manifolds with Positive First Chern Degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.34998v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every integer $n\ge5$, we construct a closed aspherical symplectic manifold of real dimension $2n$ with positive first Chern degree. Each example is a flat torus bundle over the same compact hyperbolic surface, with arithmetic monodromy arising from an explicit indefinite quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$. We identify its symplectic first Chern class with the pullback of the canonical class of the base and compute its degree explicitly. Asphericity rules out nonconstant pseudoholomorphic spheres for every tame almost complex structure. Thus these examples give a negative answer to the symplectic uniruledness question of Boucksom--Demailly--P\u{a}un--Peternell in every even real dimension at least ten.
item.dc:creator: Jingcao Wu

item.title: The $C^0$-inextendibility of Kerr spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35012v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the $C^0$-inextendibility of the full Kerr realizations considered in this paper and all their connected covering spacetimes. The result holds for positive mass and nonzero rotation in the subextremal, extremal, and overextremal regimes. The obstruction at the singular ring is expressed by unbounded proper time in a fixed-endpoint causal homotopy class. It persists under every positive continuous conformal rescaling and under continuous widening of the Kerr causal cones, without any global causality assumption. We give sharp bounds in a fixed coordinate norm for stationary and axisymmetric perturbations and describe complete timelike geodesics that encounter arbitrarily large curvature near the ring.
item.dc:creator: Bobby Eka Gunara

item.title: Type-II Singularities of Immersed Locally Convex Curves Evolving under Generalized Anisotropic Gage Area-Preserving Flows with Slow Curvature Speeds
item.description: arXiv:2610.35064v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the singularity behavior of immersed locally convex closed plane curves evolving under generalized anisotropic Gage area-preserving flows with slow curvature speeds of the form $\kappa_\sigma^\alpha$, where $0<\alpha\le 1$. Here $\kappa_\sigma$ denotes the anisotropic curvature associated with a prescribed anisotropy function $\sigma$. We prove that every finite-time blow-up is of Type-II provided that the Euclidean length of the evolving curve remains uniformly bounded away from zero. This result holds without any symmetry assumptions on either the initial curve or the anisotropy. When the initial signed area is nonzero, this length lower bound is automatically satisfied, and thus any finite-time singularity is necessarily of Type-II. By means of Hamilton's rescaling method combined with a differential Harnack estimate, we show that along a suitable blow-up subsequence, the rescaled curves at the selected times converge locally to the profile of a translating solution of the corresponding anisotropic curvature flow $V=\kappa_\sigma^\alpha$. We also establish sufficient conditions for finite-time singularity formation in terms of the initial signed area and anisotropic length. Moreover, we construct locally convex initial curves arbitrarily close to the Wulff curve for which a finite-time Type-II singularity occurs.
item.dc:creator: Ze-Yu Ye, Xiao-Liu Wang

item.title: General Relativity for Mathematicians - Part I
item.description: arXiv:2610.35194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: These notes cover the first part of a course of the same title taught by Filippo Fila-Robattino and Manuel Tecchiolli at the University of Zurich in the Winter Semester of 2025. Topics include variational principles in classical mechanics, special relativity, smooth manifolds and tensor calculus, connections and curvature, geodesic motion, and the derivation of Einstein's equations from the Einstein-Hilbert action. The treatment is aimed at a mathematical audience, combining physical motivation with precise definitions, detailed proofs, and explicit calculations.
item.dc:creator: Filippo Fila-Robattino, Manuel Tecchiolli

item.title: Log-Concavity and Fundamental Gaps on Complex Projective Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.35431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove quantitative log-concavity and fundamental-gap estimates for Dirichlet Schr\"odinger operators on complex projective domains. With holomorphic sectional curvature four, the boundary condition $\mathrm{II}\ge\sqrt{44/5}\,g$ suffices in every complex dimension under $\operatorname{Hess} V\ge2|\nabla V|g$ and $\operatorname{osc}V\le4n$. It yields $\operatorname{Hess}(-\log\phi_1)>g$ and $\lambda_2-\lambda_1>\max\{n+2+\sqrt{n^2+5n+11},\,2n+14/3\}$. The main difficulty is to control the distinguished Hopf direction together with a transverse Hessian block whose dimension grows with $n$. We extend modified-Hessian first-contact arguments by retaining the Hopf term and using longitudinal and transverse rotational tests. A trace minimization reduces all gradient orientations to three extreme directions. A dimension-scaled logarithmic barrier then compares their contact costs with a single limiting profile. A radial spectral estimate supplies the required quadratic-in-dimension spectral threshold from a dimension-independent boundary curvature bound. For $n\ge3$ these are, to our knowledge, the first log-concavity estimates for domains in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ without symmetry assumptions. We also prove a sharp diameter bound and Hessian levels linear in $n$ under larger dimension-free curvature bounds.
item.dc:creator: Gunhee Cho

item.title: Symplectic singularity as hyperK\"ahler cone
item.description: arXiv:2610.35510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that any symplectic singularity has a structure of hyperK\"ahler cone. In particular, it is equivalent to the vertex of a conical symplectic variety, and it is automatically K-polystable.
item.dc:creator: Yuji Odaka

item.title: Geometric aspects of fault tolerance
item.description: arXiv:2610.35513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We highlight three geometric aspects of fault tolerance. First, we construct an operator-algebraic formulation of the fiber bundle framework for fault tolerance, and show that a generalization of the Knill-Laflamme conditions implies a flat connection for this framework. Next, we develop this framework for Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. We show that, for each polarization type, their moduli space embeds smoothly into a Grassmannian of finite-dimensional subspaces of a regularized distribution space. Finally, we explain how GKP codes associated with Jacobians give rise to magic states that can be obtained by code space projections of Gaussian states and identify a $\rm CCZ$-type magic state arising this way.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Conrad

item.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
item.description: arXiv:2610.35534v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Elhamdadi, Bryce Virgin

item.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.35669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A string couples to a two-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For global phases, topological and index invariants, and twisted-sheaf moduli, established equivalences give alternative descriptions through cocycles, bundles, operators, or modules, with the required global compatibility data. For three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation expresses the partition function as a sum of partition functions of ordinary finite-group gauge theories. An invertible local substitution reduces invariant classical actions for a class of 2-bundle connections represented by finite-dimensional crossed modules to ordinary gauge and tensor dynamics. These finite and local reductions explicitly eliminate field variables. A four-dimensional quadratic example instead admits a direct cochain evaluation even when an ordinary gauge-theory reduction fails. These results therefore do not require the additional 2-bundle presentation.
item.dc:creator: Ferreira Bastien

item.title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.35809v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We announce a structure theory for measures on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic distance. Our results include a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability by Jones square functions, and sharp results for $L^p$ beta numbers. The results hold in every parabolic dimension and extend the theories of Edelen--Naber--Valtorta, Azzam--Tolsa and David--Semmes to space-time. The stated theorems and corollaries, together with their proofs, are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib.
item.dc:creator: Robert Koirala

item.title: Characteristic gluing to extremal Kerr horizons and the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.35836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a non-perturbative, non-axisymmetric characteristic gluing theorem for the Einstein vacuum equations: every Boyer-Lindquist sphere in the domain of outer communication of a Kerr black hole, in particular every symmetry sphere of a Schwarzschild exterior, can be glued along a single outgoing null hypersurface to a horizon sphere of an extremal Kerr black hole of sufficiently large mass. The gluing is exact at both ends and matches the full sphere data, including the transversal curvature. This proves a conjecture of Kehle and Unger in the extremal case. We first raise the angular momentum to the extremal value by rotating shear pulses of non-axisymmetric gravitational radiation, and then damp the incoming data exponentially along a long non-expanding neck. At the degenerate target horizon we invert the linearised problem at all angular frequencies, using a factorisation of a fourth-order angular operator into an angular Teukolsky-Starobinsky product. As an application, we construct one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data whose maximal development contains an exactly Schwarzschild apparent horizon and, at a later advanced time, an exactly extremal Kerr event horizon. This is the first rigorous counterexample to the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum, and proves a second conjecture of Kehle and Unger.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Czimek

item.title: Milnor fibrations and regularity conditions for real analytic mappings
item.description: arXiv:1604.05290v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When f : R power n to R power p, is a surjective real analytic map with isolated critical value, we prove that the (m)-regularity condition (in a sense we define) ensures that f ||f|| is a fibration on small spheres, f induces a fibration on the tubes and both fibrations are equivalent. In particular, we make the statement of [12] more precise in the case of isolated critical point and we extend it to the case of an isolated critical value.
item.dc:creator: J. Seade, K. Shabbir, J. Snoussi

item.title: Synthetic geometry of differential equations: I. Jets and comonad structure
item.description: arXiv:1701.06238v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an abstract formulation of the formal theory partial differential equations (PDEs) in synthetic differential geometry, one that would seamlessly generalize the traditional theory to a range of enhanced contexts, such as super-geometry, higher (stacky) differential geometry, or even a combination of both. A motivation for such a level of generality is the eventual goal of solving the open problem of covariant geometric pre-quantization of locally variational field theories, which may include fermions and (higher) gauge fields. (abridged)
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Geometry and Physics v.231 (2027) p.106025
item.dc:creator: Igor Khavkine, Urs Schreiber

item.title: Characterizations of the plane and the catenoid as capillary minimal surfaces
item.description: arXiv:1905.07887v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove that an immersed annular capillary minimal surface outside the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with one complete embedded end and finite total curvature must be either part of the plane or part of the catenoid. The proofs are based on the use of the Weierstrass data through the Hopf differential and associated holomorphic functions. For a planar end, we control the second fundamental form, while for a catenoidal end, we analyze the Gauss map in more detail using the boundary condition. We also prove nonexistence results for annular free boundary minimal surfaces with one end asymptotic to the end of Enneper's surface, under appropriate conditions. Finally, we establish an exterior analogue of Choe's result on capillary minimal surfaces with vertices.
item.dc:creator: Eungbeom Yeon

item.title: Non-Archimedean analogue of the space of valuations on convex sets
item.description: arXiv:2401.09131v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the last two decades a number of structures on the classical space of translation invariant valuations on convex bodies were discovered, e.g. product, convolution, a Fourier type transform. In this paper a non-Archimedean analogue of the space of such (even) valuations with similar structures is constructed. It is shown that, like in the classical case, the new space equipped with either product or convolution satisfies Poincar\'e duality and hard Lefschetz theorem.
item.dc:creator: Semyon Alesker

item.title: A characterization of Pfaffian embeddings from (2, 3, 5)- into flat (4, 7)-geometries
item.description: arXiv:2404.14988v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given two smooth manifolds with tangent subbundle distributions, an embedding is Pfaffian if its differential sends the distribution on the source into the distribution on the target. In this paper, we consider the question of existence of Pfaffian embeddings in the specific case where the source is a (2,3,5)-manifold, the target is the 7-dimensional space of isotropic 2-planes in a 6-dimensional symplectic vector space, and the Pfaffian condition is that the derived 3-distribution on the source be mapped into the natural 4-distribution on the target. This is one of the simpler non-trivial cases of the general question on existence of Pfaffian embeddings, but already the answer here requires solution of an interesting differential equation. It turns out that a generic (2,3,5)-manifold does not embed, the first obstruction being the fact that a Pfaffian embeddable (2,3,5)-manifold necessarily has a double root for its Cartan quartic at each point. We determine a complete characterization of embeddable (2,3,5)-manifolds in terms of their associated Cartan geometries, which characterization depends on higher order (non-harmonic) curvature as well.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin B. McMillan

item.title: Henneberg-Type Minimal Immersions in $\mathbb{R}^4$
item.description: arXiv:2512.07852v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a family of higher-order Henneberg-type minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ from explicit holomorphic data in a generalized Weierstrass--Enneper representation. The construction retains the polynomial reciprocal structure of the classical Henneberg data and yields explicit holomorphic primitives and real parametrizations for the family $\mathcal H_{(m,n)}$. We distinguish regular points from branch points, analyze the role of the complex parameter $\lambda$, and show that the real-$\lambda$ subfamily $\mathcal H_{(1,1)}$ lies in a three-dimensional linear subspace. For $\mathcal H_{(1,1)}$, we compute the induced conformal metric and Gaussian curvature, proving that the curvature is negative at every regular point. An explicit parametrization is given for $\mathcal H_{(1,1)}$, together with three-dimensional coordinate projections used solely for visualization. We also derive an integral-free formulation in terms of a single holomorphic seed function and identify the exceptional values $\lambda=\pm i$ for the inverse reconstruction formula.
item.dc:creator: Erhan G\"uler, Magdalena Toda

item.title: Curvature of left-invariant complex Finsler metric on Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2512.24791v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be an even-dimensional connected real Lie group admitting a left-invariant complex structure $J$. Let $\mathfrak g$ be the Lie algebra of $G$, and $\mathfrak g^{1,0}$ the $(1,0)$-part of the complexification $\mathfrak g^{\mathbb{C}}$ of $\mathfrak g$. We derive explicit formulas for the holomorphic sectional curvature and holomorphic bisectional curvature of any left-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric $F$ on $G$, expressed in terms of the complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g^{1,0}$. We also obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for $F$ to be a K\"ahler-Finsler metric (resp. weakly K\"ahler-Finsler metric). As an application, we prove a rigidity result: if $G$ is a complex Lie group and $F$ is a left-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric on $G$, then $F$ must be a complex Berwald metric with vanishing holomorphic bisectional curvature; moreover, $F$ is a K\"ahler-Berwald metric if and only if $G$ is an abelian complex Lie group.
item.dc:creator: Kuankuan Luo, Wei Xiao, Chunping Zhong

item.title: Pluriclosed 3-folds with vanishing Bismut Ricci form: General theory in the quasi-regular case
item.description: arXiv:2601.04937v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study compact complex $3$-dimensional non-K\"ahler Bismut Ricci flat pluriclosed Hermitian manifolds (BHE) via their dimensional reduction to a special K\"ahler geometry in complex dimension $2$, recently obtained by Barbaro, Streets and the first and third authors. We show that in the quasi-regular case, the reduced geometry satisfies a 6th order non-linear PDE which has infinite dimensional momentum map interpretation, similar to the much studied K\"ahler metrics of constant scalar curvature (cscK). We use this to associate to the reduced manifold or orbifold Mabuchi and Calabi functionals, as well as to obtain obstructions for the existence of solutions in terms of the authomorphism group, paralleling results by Futaki and Calabi-Lichnerowicz-Matsushima in the cscK case. This is used to characterize the Samelson locally homogeneous BHE geometries in complex dimension 3 as the only non-K\"ahler BHE $3$-folds with $2$-dimensional Bott-Chern $(1,1)$-cohomology group, for which the reduced space is a smooth K\"ahler surface. We also discuss explicit solutions of the PDE on orthotoric K\"ahler orbifold surfaces, extending examples found by Couzens-Gauntlett-Martelli-Sparks in the framework of supersymmetric ${\rm AdS}_3 \times Y_7$ type IIB supergravity. Our construction yields infinitely many non-K\"ahler BHE structures on $S^3\times S^3$ and $S^1\times S^2 \times S^3$, which are not locally isometric to a Samelson geometry. These appear to be the first such examples.
item.dc:creator: Vestislav Apostolov, Abdellah Lahdili, Kuan-Hui Lee

item.title: Prolongation rigidity of sub-free Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2603.01643v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that if the 0-th Tanaka prolongation $\mathfrak{g}_0=\mathfrak{der}_0(\mathfrak{m})$ of a fundamental graded nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{m}=\mathfrak{g}_{-s}\oplus\dots\oplus\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$ is irreducible on $\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$, then $\mathfrak{m}$ is prolongation rigid: $\text{pr}_+(\mathfrak{m})=0$. The only exceptions are given by negative gradations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of a simple Lie algebra.
item.dc:creator: Boris Kruglikov

item.title: On the existence of toric ALE and ALF gravitational instantons
item.description: arXiv:2604.15159v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish existence and uniqueness results for asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) and asymptotically locally flat (ALF) gravitational instantons. In particular, we prove the existence of a unique, Ricci-flat, toric ALE and ALF gravitational instanton, for every admissible rod structure, that is smooth up to possible conical singularites. We also give an elementary proof that any toric ALE or ALF self-dual instanton is a multi-Eguchi-Hanson or multi-Taub-NUT solution.
item.dc:creator: Hari K. Kunduri, James Lucietti

item.title: Existence of rotationally symmetric embedded f-minimal tori
item.description: arXiv:2605.05022v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $n\geq2$, and let $f:[0,+\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth function satisfying $f''\geq0$ and $0<m\leq f'\leq M$ for some constants $m$ and $M$. We prove that $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, endowed with the conformal metric \begin{equation*} ds^2=e^{-\frac{f(|x|^2)}{2n}}\sum_{i=1}^{n+1}dx_i^2, \end{equation*} admits a compact, embedded, rotationally symmetric minimal hypersurface diffeomorphic to $S^1\times S^{n-1}$. This extends Angenent's existence theorem for self-shrinking tori, which is recovered when $f(s)=s$.
item.dc:creator: Peng Peng

item.title: Isoperimetric and total curvature inequalities in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with nullity
item.description: arXiv:2605.24638v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using the Chern-Gauss-Bonnet theorem, we establish a sharp inequality for the total Gauss-Kronecker curvature of convex hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds $M^n$ with nullity index at least $n-3$. Consequently, the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality extends to $M^n$, which proves the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture for these spaces.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Ghomi

item.title: A note on the cohomology of pullback Lie algebroids
item.description: arXiv:2607.23859v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a direct differential-geometric proof of a result of Crainic on the cohomology of pullbacks of Lie algebroids under surjective submersions: If the fibers are connected and have vanishing cohomology through degree $n$, pullback with coefficients in any representation is an isomorphism through degree $n$ and is injective in degree $n+1$. The proof reduces to a vanishing result for leafwise cohomology and uses an exhaustion-and-patching argument due to Buchdahl. No local triviality or finite-type assumption on the fibers is required. We also prove the analogous result for holomorphic Lie algebroids.
item.dc:creator: Eckhard Meinrenken

item.title: Failure of the local decay formula for Arnold multiplicities under twisted K\"ahler--Ricci flow
item.description: arXiv:2608.30302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu asked whether local Arnold multiplicities under maximal weak twisted K\"ahler--Ricci flow with fixed cohomology class satisfy $\lambda(\varphi_t,x)=\max\{\lambda(\varphi_0,x)-t,0\}$. We construct counterexamples with analytic initial singularities in every dimension $n\ge2$. On the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$, $e\ge2$, the initial current $[S]+(e+1)[F]$ yields $\lambda(\varphi_t,x)=1/2-t/e$ for $x\in S\setminus F$ and $0<t<e/2$, where $S$ is the negative section and $F$ a fibre. Products with smooth stationary factors give higher-dimensional examples. The Zariski negative part of $\{S\}+\{F\}$, the reduced support class, forces extra divisor mass. For pure divisorial data with simple normal crossings support, a smooth semipositive representative of the reduced support class's positive part gives exact short-time formulas. On one surface we construct flows with identical initial current germs, background data and global initial Arnold multiplicity, but different local rates.
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin

item.title: Free boundary minimal surfaces of genus zero
item.description: arXiv:2609.13054v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that any embedded genus zero free boundary minimal surface in the ball has first Steklov eigenvalue $1$. This implies the uniqueness of the critical catenoid.
item.dc:creator: Otis Chodosh, Matilde Gianocca

item.title: Biharmonic Conformal Immersions of Hypersurfaces: Dirac Rigidity and Mixed Clifford Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2609.20197v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A biharmonic conformal immersion asks whether a hypersurface can become a critical point of the bienergy after a conformal change of the domain metric. We study when this flexibility can produce compact nonconstant-mean-curvature geometry in space forms. For surfaces in three-dimensional space forms, with $U=\lambda^2H$, Ou's system is encoded exactly by a Laplace-type operator acting on a restricted ambient Killing spinor. We classify all monic scalar--chiral factorizations of this operator. In nonzero curvature such a factorization exists locally exactly when the principal curvatures are locally constant; the normalized Euclidean branch is equally rigid, and the remaining real spherical non-CMC branch is excluded by a finite-type Frobenius obstruction. For $m>2$, this scalar rigidity does not imply geometric nonexistence. The conformal tension has independent normal and tangential components. We prove that $\mathbb R\xi\oplus TM$ is the minimal natural $O(m)$-equivariant carrier, derive the corresponding strongly elliptic Jacobi block and its two-grade Clifford realization, and identify off-diagonal hybridization as the escape mechanism. Exact cohomogeneity-one reductions, combined with validated interval and Chebyshev/radii-polynomial arguments, yield embedded proper non-CMC, nowhere-umbilical examples in round spheres, including $$ S^1\times\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb S^n\hookrightarrow\mathbb S^{2n+2} \qquad(n\ge1). $$ Thus the scalar obstruction is sharp with respect to coefficient bundle: the smallest enlargement forced by conformal tension already supports compact non-CMC solutions.
item.dc:creator: Dipesh Bhandari

item.title: Non-maximal quasi-isometric $\mathrm{PU}_{2,n+1}$-representations via alternating surfaces in complex pseudo-hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.24672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every admissible non-maximal Toledo invariant $t$, we construct a locus of irreducible representations of a closed genus-$g$ surface group into $\mathrm{PU}_{2,n+1}$ with Toledo invariant $t$ whose orbit maps are quasi-isometric embeddings. These loci have real codimension $10(g-1)$ or $10(g-1)+2(n-1)$ in the character variety depending on the Toledo value. Our construction uses $4$-cyclic Higgs bundles and their correspondence with $\partial$-alternating surfaces in complex pseudo-hyperbolic spaces. The associated equivariant minimal maps into the symmetric space are bi-Lipschitz embeddings. We further construct cocompact domains of discontinuity in the Shilov boundary. Their quotients are smooth fiber bundles over the surface with fiber homeomorphic to $S^{2n-1}\times S^{2n-1}$.
item.dc:creator: Qiongling Li, Junming Zhang

item.title: Gromov-Hausdorff instability of the positive mass theorem for K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.32383v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a sequence of AE K\"ahler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^2$ with nonnegative and integrable scalar curvature whose ADM mass tends to zero but which, for a suitable choice of basepoints, fails to converge to Euclidean space in the pointed Gromov-Hausdorff sense.
item.dc:creator: Romy Marie Merkel

item.title: Positive sectional curvature on a family of exotic fifteen-sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.03310v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature on at least 508 pairwise nondiffeomorphic exotic fifteen-spheres, without prescribing orientations. The construction begins with quaternionic line bundles over $\mathbb{H}P^2\times S^4$. Surgery along a Hopf fiber gives homotopy spheres with specified equivariant two-disk presentations. A calculation on the surgery filling distinguishes 1015 nonstandard oriented smooth types. We construct positively curved quotient metrics on both disks, match their boundary data under the prescribed attaching map, and smooth the seam by averaging the inverse tangential metrics. The connection estimates and the smoothing argument are proved directly for every two-plane. Thus the curvature conclusion does not require a compatible-disk theorem from the eleven-dimensional construction or an external curvature-gluing theorem. We give quantitative parameter bounds and specify the auxiliary choices for the first nontrivial member after fixing its smooth gauge family.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqi Chen, Shaoqiang Deng, Hui Zhang

item.title: A curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form of a regular surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and its applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.10132v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a Monge normal form of a surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ based on the principal axes of its curvature ellipse. The curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form is obtained using only Euclidean motions of the ambient space and local reparameterizations of the surface, and preserves the Euclidean invariants of the curvature ellipse, including its semi-axis lengths up to their ordering. We also give applications of this normal form to the $2$-jet geometry of surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and to the geometry of their orthogonal projections.
item.dc:creator: Masaru Hasegawa

item.title: Non-algebraicity of the Lawson surfaces $\xi_{k,l}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.16853v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every Lawson surface $\xi_{k,l}\subset\mathbb S^3$ of genus $kl>1$ is non-algebraic: any real polynomial vanishing on $\xi_{k,l}$ vanishes identically on $\mathbb S^3$. This answers a question posed by Hsiang in 1967 and proves Lawson's 1970 conjecture for $\xi_{2,2}$. The proof uses a reflection principle for the monodromy of the associated family of flat connections.
item.dc:creator: Lynn Heller, Sebastian Heller

item.title: On flat metric nilpotent Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.23481v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study flat left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics on nilpotent Lie groups. Associated with a flat metric Lie algebra $(\mathfrak{g},\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ there is a canonical affine action of the corresponding group on the vector space $\mathfrak{g}$, whose linear part is the Levi-Civita representation $L$. Combining this action with Scheuneman's theorem on pure translations in nilpotent affine groups, we prove that a flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra has a nontrivial kernel of $L$, that is, $\ker L\neq 0$. As a consequence, every $n$-dimensional flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra is a double extension of an $(n-2)$-dimensional flat metric nilpotent Lie algebra.
item.dc:creator: Huihui An, Zaili Yan, Hui Zhang, Shaoxiang Zhang

item.title: On Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28651v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we introduce a class of non-flat Lorentzian manifolds, called Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds (briefly, LTFSMs). This class contains Lorentzian concircular structure manifolds (briefly, LCSMs), LSP-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds with coefficient $\alpha$, LP-$\alpha$-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds, and LP-$\alpha$-Kenmotsu manifolds. The interrelations among these various classes of manifolds are illustrated in Figures 1 and 2.
