We investigate several geometric properties of LTFSMs. In particular, we show that the expansion scalar, given by the divergence of $\xi$, is nonzero and nonconstant, and that the flow of $\xi$ is irrotational. In an LCSM, the Ricci operator commutes with the structure tensor $\phi$ [12]. However, it is shown that, in an LTFSM, the Ricci operator does not generally commute with $\phi$. If the gradient of the torse-forming scalar $\alpha$ is collinear with the torse-forming vector field $\xi$, then the Ricci operator commutes with $\phi$, and the manifold reduces to an LCSM. It is known that a conformally flat LCSM is quasi-Einstein and hence is a manifold of quasi-constant curvature. We show that a conformally flat LTFSM is a generalized quasi-Einstein manifold in the sense of Chaki [1] and is also a manifold of generalized quasi-constant curvature. Several curvature-related properties of LTFSMs are established, and their sectional curvature is determined. The existence of LTFSMs is demonstrated through several proper nontrivial examples. We also present examples that are simultaneously LCSMs and LTFSMs, examples of LTFMs characterizing twisted cubic spacetimes, and generalized Robertson-Walker (GRW) spacetimes characterizing LCSMs. Finally, we provide examples of LTFSMs in which the vector field $\xi$ is a unit timelike torse-forming vector field but is not concircular; see Examples 5.6--5.8.
item.dc:creator: Absos Ali Shaikh

item.title: Kodaira-type Vanishings via Non-abelian Hodge Theory
item.description: arXiv:2207.09064v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we use nonabelian Hodge theory to study Kodaira-type vanishings. In particular, we generalize Saito vanishing using mixed twistor $\sD$-modules. We also generalize it to a Kawamata-Viehweg type vanishing using $\Q$-divisors, and prove an effective global generation theorem, as an application. We also prove a relative vanishing for a projective morphism in the mixed twistor $\sD$-module setting.
item.dc:creator: Chuanhao Wei

item.title: A theory of stratification learning
item.description: arXiv:2405.20066v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given i.i.d. sample from a stratified mixture of immersed manifolds of different dimensions, we study the minimax estimation of the underlying stratified structure. We provide a constructive algorithm allowing to estimate each mixture component at its optimal dimension-specific rate adaptively. The method is based on an ascending hierarchical co-detection of points belonging to different layers, which also identifies the number of layers and their dimensions, assigns each data point to a layer accurately, and estimates tangent spaces optimally. These results hold regardless of any ambient assumption on the manifolds or on their intersection configurations. They open the way to a broad clustering framework, where each mixture component models a cluster emanating from a specific nonlinear correlation phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Eddie Aamari, Cl\'ement Berenfeld

item.title: On cutoff via rigidity for high dimensional curved diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2412.15969v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider overdamped Langevin diffusions in Euclidean space, with curvature equal to the spectral gap. This includes the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process as well as non-Gaussian and non-product extensions with convex interaction, such as the Dyson process from random matrix theory. We show that a cutoff phenomenon or abrupt convergence to equilibrium occurs in high dimension, at a critical time equal to the logarithm of the dimension divided by twice the spectral gap. This cutoff holds for Wasserstein distance, total variation, relative entropy, and Fisher information. A key observation is a relation to a spectral rigidity, linked to the presence of a Gaussian factor. A novelty is the extensive usage of functional inequalities, even for short-time regularization, and the reduction to Wasserstein. The proofs are short and conceptual. Since the product condition is satisfied, an Lp cutoff holds for all finite p. We moreover discuss a natural extension to Riemannian manifolds, a link with logarithmic gradient estimates in short-time for the heat kernel, and ask about stability by perturbation. Finally, beyond rigidity but still for diffusions, a discussion around the recent progress on the product condition for non-negatively curved diffusions leads us to introduce a new curvature product condition.
item.dc:creator: Djalil Chafa\"i, Max Fathi

item.title: Low Genus Curves on Compact Shimura Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2502.11582v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate and compare the behaviors of complex curves on two major types of compact Shimura surfaces: compact variants of Picard and Hilbert modular surfaces. They are quotients of complex hyperbolic balls corresponding to moduli problems for abelian varieties with certain endomorphism types. We prove that if we fix a genus bound, then when the defining discriminant is large enough, low genus curves on the compact variant of Picard modular surfaces do not exist, while low genus curves may persist on the compact variant of Hilbert modular surfaces only if they are special curves, which parametrize those with extra endomorphisms. These results are special cases of a complex function field analogue of uniform boundedness on endomorphism types of abelian varieties. The proof requires understanding the repulsion of special subvarieties and relies on volume estimates in hyperbolic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Zhehao Li

item.title: Conformal Green functions and Yamabe metrics of Sobolev regularity
item.description: arXiv:2507.01674v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a full resolution of the Yamabe problem on closed 3-manifolds for Riemannian metrics of Sobolev class $W^{2,q}$ with $q > 3$. This requires developing an elliptic theory for the conformal Laplacian for rough metrics and establishing existence, regularity and a delicate blow-up analysis for its Green function. Most of the analytical work is carried out in dimensions $n \geq 3$ and for $W^{2,q}$ Riemannian metrics with $q>\tfrac{n}{2}$ and should be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Avalos, Albachiara Cogo, Andoni Royo Abrego

item.title: On the Dirichlet boundary value problem on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2601.09930v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study bounded solutions of Dirichlet boundary value problems for semilinear elliptic equations on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature. We prove nonexistence when the asymptotic boundary has zero Hausdorff measure at an exponent determined by the upper curvature bound and the spectral parameter. The result holds for continuous viscosity solutions under a one-sided bound on the nonlinearity, including the Allen-Cahn equation. The proof combines convex barriers at infinity, distance comparison for $C^{1,1}$ hypersurfaces and a spectral maximum principle. For surfaces, no lower curvature bound is needed.
item.dc:creator: Marcos P. Cavalcante, Jos\'e M. Espinar, Diego A. Mar\'in

item.title: Sharp Riemannian heat kernel estimates on the cut locus and the Parabolic Anderson model
item.description: arXiv:2603.26936v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using sharp global heat kernel bounds and geodesic comparison geometry, we show that the Dalang condition for well-posedness of the parabolic Anderson model with measure-valued initial conditions, first introduced on Euclidean space, holds on general compact Riemannian manifolds. We furthermore establish upper and lower moment bounds for all such solutions, providing evidence for intermittency in this generality. This extends and simplifies earlier work that required non-positive curvature.
item.dc:creator: Hongyi Chen, Robert Neel, Cheng Ouyang

item.title: Free maps in critical dimension on low-dimensional tori and closed surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.24610v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a method to build free immersions in critical dimension on $m$-tori for $m = 2, 3, 4, 5$ by using a factorization trick inspired by tori immersions in critical dimension. As an application, we show that the set of smooth free maps from a closed surface $M$ to $\mathbb R^5$ is nonempty. In particular, every closed surface embeds freely in $\mathbb R^5$. Finally, we find the homotopy invariants of free maps in our environment and study which invariants are achieved by our maps.
item.dc:creator: Roberto De Leo

item.title: How to Untwist Twisted Gauge Fields
item.description: arXiv:2606.28888v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper provides an isomorphism between the space of twisted gauge fields on a principal bundle $\mathcal{P}(M,H)$ and the space of standard gauge fields on a different principal bundle $\mathcal{Q}(M,G)$ associated to $\mathcal{P}$. This isomorphism extends to local fields on the base manifold, which enables the use of local twisted fields in standard gauge theories (e.g. Yang-Mills-like theories). This allows one to deal with two symmetry groups, coming from $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$, respectively. The construction makes use of a larger principal bundle $\mathcal{S}$ which has $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ as quotient bundles. $\mathcal{S}$ is a Hilsum-Skandalis bibundle between the action groupoids $H\ltimes\mathcal{P}$ and $G\ltimes\mathcal{Q}$. The gauge structure on $\mathcal{S}$ encodes both standard and twisted gauge structures on $\mathcal{P}$. In addition, the isomorphism classes of bundles $\mathcal{S}$ up to an isomorphism covering the identity map on $\mathcal{P}$ are in 1:1 correspondence with the equivalence classes of cocycles (up to a coboundary). This paper also provides a new interpretation of (full) dressing fields as dynamic (or active) sections of a principal bundle.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Serge Lazzarini, Thierry Masson, Louis Usala, How to untwist twisted gauge fields, Journal of Geometry and Physics, Volume 231, 2027, 106028, ISSN 0393-0440
item.dc:creator: Serge Lazzarini, Thierry Masson, Louis Usala

item.title: Surjectivity of real-linear Cauchy--Riemann operators: from the minimal Harder--Narasimhan slope to automatic transversality
item.description: arXiv:2608.18997v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper relates the minimal Harder--Narasimhan slope to the surjectivity of real-linear Cauchy--Riemann operators. We establish a conformally invariant $L^2$ criterion and an asymptotic slope criterion, which yield higher-rank automatic transversality criteria for pseudoholomorphic curves beyond the classical rank-one framework. Applications to pseudoholomorphic spheres in $S^6$ provide quantitative $L^2$ obstructions to the integrability of almost complex structures.
item.dc:creator: Qingchun Ji, Jun Yao

item.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation in higher dimensions I
item.description: arXiv:2609.28323v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We complete, in the general Riemannian setting, the classification of isolated singularities of positive solutions to the Yamabe equation for dimensions \(3\le n\le29\), initiated in the flat case by Caffarelli, Gidas, and Spruck in 1989. Precisely, every isolated singularity is either removable or the solution is asymptotic to a Fowler solution. The sharpness of this range is established by counterexamples for every dimension \(n\ge30\) in our companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Zheng-Chao Han, Qinfeng Jiang, Hua-Yang Wang, Jingang Xiong, Lei Zhang

item.title: A Half-Space Theorem for the Allen--Cahn Equation in All Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15014v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, a bounded, non-constant entire solution of the Allen--Cahn equation whose zero set is contained in a half-space is a one-dimensional heteroclinic solution.
item.dc:creator: Sanghoon Lee
